extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners; patent applicants and practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating and processing obviousness rejections under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) where disqualification of prior art under 35 U.S.C. 103(c) (common ownership or joint research agreement/CREATE Act) may apply. Covers evidence standards, examiner procedures, form paragraphs, and related double patenting treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirement for common ownership/joint research agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: The common ownership or joint research agreement must be shown to exist at the time the later invention was made. A statement of present common ownership is not sufficient. The joint research agreement must be in effect on or before the date the claimed invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An invention is 'made' when conception is complete (citing Mergenthaler v. Scudder; In re Tansel) and must also meet the Pfaff readiness-for-patenting standard (e.g., drawings or descriptions sufficiently specific to enable a person skilled in the art to practice the invention). The JRA may be in effect prior to the CREATE Act effective date and does not need to be in effect on or before the prior art date of the reference sought to be disqualified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of an applicant/attorney statement to establish common ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications and references will be considered to be owned by, or subject to an obligation of assignment to, the same person, at the time the invention was made, if the applicant(s) or an attorney or agent of record makes a statement to the effect that the application and the reference were, at the time the invention was made, owned by, or subject to an obligation of assignment to, the same person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant(s) or representative(s) of record have best knowledge and their clear, conspicuous statement (e.g., on separate paper or separately labeled section) is generally sufficient because of their obligation of candor and good faith. Example wording: 'Application X and Patent A were, at the time the invention of Application X was made, owned by Company Z.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear and conspicuous placement of common ownership statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement concerning common ownership should be clear and conspicuous (e.g., on a separate piece of paper or in a separately labeled section) to ensure that the examiner quickly notices the statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may, but are not required to, submit further objective evidence in addition to the statement. Failure to provide a conspicuous statement may render the attempted disqualification ineffective and require additional evidence per MPEP § 706.02(l).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective evidence that may be required to establish common ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner has independent evidence raising a material doubt about the accuracy of an applicant's representation of common ownership or obligation to assign, the examiner may require objective evidence of common ownership as of the date the invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable objective evidence includes: (A) reference to assignments recorded in the USPTO in accordance with 37 CFR Part 3 conveying entire rights to same person(s)/organization(s); (B) copies of unrecorded assignments conveying entire rights filed in each application; (C) an affidavit or declaration by the common owner stating common ownership and facts explaining why the affiant believes there is common ownership (signed by corporate official if owner is organization); (D) other evidence establishing common ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden to invoke 35 U.S.C. 103(c) (common ownership or JRA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an examiner has established a prima facie case of obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103(a), the burden of overcoming the rejection by invoking the joint research agreement provisions of 35 U.S.C. 103(c) as amended by the CREATE Act is on the applicant or the patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must comply with the statute and rules of practice in effect. If the applicant disqualifies the subject matter in accordance with 103(c) and procedures, the examiner will treat the application and the 102(e)/(f)/(g) prior art as if commonly owned for purposes of 103(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a Joint Research Agreement (103(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 103(c)(3) defines a 'joint research agreement' as a written contract, grant, or cooperative agreement entered into by two or more persons or entities for the performance of experimental, developmental, or research work in the field of the claimed invention, that was in effect on or before the date the claimed invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The claimed invention must have been made as a result of activities undertaken within the scope of the JRA. A JRA limited to activities for a different, distinct invention does not qualify to disqualify the later reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence required to establish a Joint Research Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: To overcome a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) based upon subject matter which qualifies as prior art under only one or more of 35 U.S.C. 102(e), (f), or (g) via the CREATE Act, the applicant must comply with the statute and the rules of practice in effect and submit appropriate evidence showing the JRA was in effect and the invention was made within its scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant attempts to disqualify a reference under 103(c) using the JRA provisions but fails to submit required items, the examiner must include form paragraph 7.20.05 and identify the missing requirements (see 37 CFR 1.71(g) and 1.104(c) and MPEP § 706.02(l)). Examples in the MPEP illustrate circumstances where JRA timing or scope defeats the disqualification attempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner procedure when reference is not shown disqualified under 103(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application file being examined has not established that the reference is disqualified as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 103(c), the examiner will assume the reference is not disqualified and proceed accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically the examiner will: (A) assume the reference is not disqualified; (B) examine the application on all grounds other than any conflict between the reference patent(s) or application(s) arising from a possible 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection based on 102(e),(f),(g); (C) consider applicability of any references under 103 based on 102(e),(f),(g), including provisional rejections under 102(e)/103; (D) apply the best references against the claimed invention by rejections under 102 and 103, including 102(e)/103 rejections, until the reference is disqualified under 103(c). The examiner should anticipate that a 102(e)/103 reference may be disqualified under 103(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner procedure when reference is established disqualified under 103(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application being examined has established that the reference is disqualified as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 103(c), the examiner will alter examination accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner will: (A) examine the applications as to all grounds except 35 U.S.C. 102(e), (f), and (g) as they apply through 103, including provisional rejections under 102(e)/103; (B) examine the applications for double patenting, including statutory and nonstatutory double patenting, and make a provisional rejection if appropriate; (C) invite the applicant to file a terminal disclaimer to overcome any provisional or actual nonstatutory double patenting rejection, if appropriate (see 37 CFR 1.321).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of commonly owned applications of different inventive entities (double patenting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commonly owned applications of different inventive entities may be rejected on the ground of double patenting, even if the later filed application claims 35 U.S.C. 120 benefit to the earlier application. The CREATE Act amendment may cause double patenting rejections between applications not owned by the same party by treating the subject matter disqualified under 103(c) as if commonly owned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double patenting rejections can be overcome in certain circumstances by disclaiming, pursuant to 37 CFR 1.321, the terminal portion of the later patent's term and including a provision that the patent shall be enforceable only for and during the period the patent is commonly owned with the application or patent which formed the basis for the rejection. For a double patenting rejection based on a non-commonly owned patent treated as commonly owned pursuant to the CREATE Act, the double patenting rejection may be obviated by filing a terminal disclaimer in accordance with 37 CFR 1.321(d). See MPEP § 804 and § 804.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rejection criteria for copending applications (7.21.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use paragraph 7.21.01 to provisionally reject claims not patentably distinct from the disclosure in a copending application having an earlier U.S. filing date and also having either a common assignee or at least one common inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provisional rejection assumes future publication or patenting of the copending application (which would make it prior art under 102(e)). The provisional rejection may be overcome by: (1) a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that any invention disclosed but not claimed in the copending application was derived from the inventor of this application; (2) showing a date of invention for the instant application prior to the effective U.S. filing date of the copending application under 37 CFR 1.131; or (3) showing that the copending application is disqualified under 103(c). Do not use this paragraph where the copending application is disqualified under 103(c) as prior art in a 103(a) rejection pursuant to 103(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: When a reference that is attempted to be disqualified still qualifies under another 102 subsection
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reference qualifies as prior art under another subsection of 35 U.S.C. 102 (e.g., 102(a) or 102(b)) it is not disqualified under 103(c) even if an applicant attempts to show common ownership or a JRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.20.01 must be used following form paragraph 7.20 in all actions containing rejections under 103(a) using art that is disqualified under 103(c) using 102(e),(f),(g) but which qualifies under another section of 102. Applicant may instead antedate under 37 CFR 1.131 or show derivation under 37 CFR 1.132.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph use and examiner notes for 103(a) rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: The MPEP provides specific form paragraphs (¶ 7.20, 7.20.01, 7.20.02, 7.20.04, 7.20.05, 7.21, 7.21.01, 7.21.02, etc.) that should be used in making appropriate rejections and communications concerning 35 U.S.C. 103(a) and related 103(c) issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the examiner notes for when each paragraph is required (e.g., ¶7.20 is required in first actions on the merits employing 103(a) and final rejections; ¶7.20.02 must be used in all applications with joint inventors unless claims are clearly restricted). Use ¶7.20.04 when applicant attempted to disqualify a reference via common ownership but failed to provide a conspicuous statement. Use ¶7.20.05 when attempt to use JRA provisions fails to meet statutory/rule requirements. Precede certain paragraphs with 7.20 or 7.103 per instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner expectation regarding possible later disqualification
rubrics_metrics.description: When applying any 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103 references against the claims, the examiner should anticipate that the reference may be disqualified under 35 U.S.C. 103(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a statement of common ownership or assignment is filed in reply to the 102(e)/103 rejection and the claims are not amended, the examiner may not make the next Office action final if a new rejection is made (see MPEP § 706.07(a)). However, if the reference is disqualified under the JRA provision and a new subsequent double patenting rejection based upon the disqualified reference is applied, the next Office action containing the new double patenting rejection may be made final (subject to caveats in the text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graham v. Deere factual inquiries for obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: The factual inquiries set forth in Graham v. John Deere Co., that are applied for establishing a background for determining obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) are summarized as: 1. Determining the scope and contents of the prior art. 2. Ascertaining the differences between the prior art and the claims at issue. 3. Resolving the level of ordinary skill in the pertinent art. 4. Considering objective evidence present in the application indicating obviousness or nonobviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An explanation of the rejection applying the Graham test must follow form paragraph 7.21. This form paragraph may be used, if appropriate, in response to an argument invoking Graham v. Deere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 35 U.S.C. 102(e) date rules (AIPA / pre-AIPA distinctions)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a rejection relies upon prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e), examiners must use 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as amended by the American Inventors Protection Act (AIPA) to determine the reference's prior art date, unless the reference is a U.S. patent issued directly or indirectly from an international application with an international filing date prior to November 29, 2000 (pre-AIPA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pre-AIPA 102(e) only if the reference is a U.S. patent issued from an international application filed prior to November 29, 2000 or a continuing application claiming benefit to such an international application. See Examiner Notes for form paragraphs 7.12 and 7.12.01 for assistance in determining the 102(e) date.

rubrics_metrics.name: What to do when applicant fails to provide required common-ownership/JRA evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant has attempted to disqualify a reference under 103(c) but has failed to provide the required statement or other necessary evidence, the reference is not disqualified as prior art under 103(a) and the applicant must file the required evidence to properly disqualify the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must include the appropriate form paragraph (e.g., 7.20.04 for common ownership failures, 7.20.05 for JRA failures) identifying the deficiency and advise applicant of alternative ways to overcome the applied art (e.g., derivation under 37 CFR 1.132 or antedating under 37 CFR 1.131).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of common ownership for joint inventors (¶ 7.20.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application currently names joint inventors, the examiner presumes that the subject matter of the various claims was commonly owned at the time any inventions covered therein were made absent evidence to the contrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is advised of the obligation under 37 CFR 1.56 to point out inventor and invention dates of each claim that was not commonly owned at the time a later invention was made so the examiner can consider applicability of 35 U.S.C. 103(c) and potential 102(e)/(f)/(g) prior art under 103(a). This paragraph must be used in all applications with joint inventors unless claims are clearly restricted to only one claimed invention.
